To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified three new Spanish cases of GAMT deficiency and we have described the clinical features and response to therapy of these patients, as well as the comparison with other published cases of the same disease.
GAMT deficiency should be considered as a cause of mental retardation, movement disorders and epilepsy in children, and that early diagnosis and treatment is important.
we present the first Spanish patients with GAMTs deficiency, and we describe the clinical features and the response to treatment of these patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a group of rare diseases, but with a high impact in patients and families, and with an important therapeutic potential.
the study of the molecular and biochemical bases of the inborn errors of the metabolism.
the study of the clinical, biochemical, genetic, and therapeutic aspects of GAMT deficiency, which is a new metabolic disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the GAMT deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder, with a variable phenotype that can include mental retardation, seizures and/or movement disorders, with the presence of guanidinacetate in urine and low levels of Cr in brain magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and that can be treated with oral Cr supplementation.
GAMT deficiency is the cause of a specific clinical entity characterized by a triad of mental retardation, movement disorder and epilepsy, and that the treatment with Cr is beneficial.

the clinical spectrum of patients with GAMT-deficiency is wide, but the diagnosis of GAMT-deficiency in patients with mental impairment and/or epilepsy should be considered, especially in those with movement disorder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GAMT deficiency should be included in the differential diagnosis for mental retardation of unexplained aetiology, especially when there is a movement disorder or epilepsy.
the diagnosis of GAMT deficiency should be considered when patients with mental retardations, epilepsy and movement disorders present with low brain creatine levels.
GAMT deficiency should be considered as a cause of mental retardation in patients with a movement disorder or epilepsy, specially in those who present autistic behaviour.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diagnosis of GAMT deficiency is not rare and should be considered in the work-up of patients with unexplained mental retardation.
the treatment with Cr is safe and effective in patients with GAMT-deficiency.
GAMT deficiency is an important cause of cerebral creatine deficiency, and that early diagnosis and treatment are crucial for a better outcome in these patients.
